|\n---IMPORTED-NATIVE---\n# Imported PPTX and nativeRef\n\nUse this route for a third-party PPTX whose unknown package content must survive\nan edit.\n\n```bash\nofficekit ppj import input.pptx -o deck.ppj\nofficekit ppj inspect deck.ppj --query \"visible title\" --json\nofficekit ppj check deck.ppj --json\nofficekit ppj build deck.ppj -o edited.pptx --json\n```\n\nImport copies the source into a content-addressed read-only asset and binds its\nSHA-256. Every visible object must appear as a typed element or an `opaque`\nelement with `nativeRef`, location, summary, and issued capabilities. Unknown\nOOXML remains in the source package and does not enter the model context.\n\n## Edit boundary\n\n- Edit ordinary PPJ fields only when the typed object has the corresponding\n  issued capability, such as `replaceText`, `setFrame`, `replaceImage`,\n  `setChartTitle`, or `setChartData`.\n- For a precise imported scalar, use an issued `nativeRef.leaves[]` entry. It\n  contains an opaque leaf ID, closed `kind`, source-value `expectedHash`, and\n  human-facing `value`. Change only `value`.\n- Never invent a leaf, copy one to another object, alter its ID/kind/hash, or\n  convert a typed operation such as image replacement into a scalar leaf.\n- Keep source revision, target hash, object identity, and page identity intact.\n- Re-import after build and locate the same stable IDs again.\n\nExample imported run-size edit:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": \"nl_8b1f…\",\n  \"kind\": \"fontSizePoints\",\n  \"expectedHash\": \"<sha256 of the exact native old value>\",\n  \"value\": 20\n}\n```\n\nThe value uses a human unit where PPJ defines one: points for font size,\ndegrees for rotation, booleans for flips, and `#RRGGBB` for direct RGB. EMU\nleaves remain explicitly named `*Emu`; they exist for exact source surgery,\nnot for ordinary authored layout.\n\nNo-op build must return the source bytes exactly. A supported edit may change\nonly the target part and necessary dependencies. Unrelated parts,\nrelationships, master/layout/theme state, unknown timing, OLE, source-owned\nSmartArt topology, and other opaque content must remain stable.\n\nSome imported shapes with a strict direct embedded `a:blipFill` and a custom\ngeometry that is not yet semantically decoded may expose a source-bound\n`imageFill` capability. This is a bounded frame-edit path: the existing image\nrelationship, crop, and custom geometry remain source-owned while the shape's\nposition or size changes. Image replacement, fill conversion, custom-path\nrewriting, and any other image-fill graph stay opaque and fail closed.\n\nAn imported shape may also expose `textEditable` while its fill or effect graph\nis intentionally opaque (for example, a native gradient banner). A plain\ntext-only replacement is safe when the original paragraph/run topology is\nkept; the native fill, effects, geometry, and relationships remain byte-owned\nby the source. Style, frame, name, and topology changes still fail closed.\n\nSource-bound connectors may expose the same bounded placement surface when\ntheir direct frame is a legal horizontal or vertical line with one zero\nextent. Moving the frame leaves endpoint bindings, line geometry, and unknown\nextension children untouched. Zero-by-zero, negative, missing, or ambiguous\nconnector frames remain read-only; this is not permission to rewrite connector\ntopology.\n\nSource-bound opaque pictures may likewise retain a bounded negative left/top\noffset when the picture frame and unique image relationship are proven safe.\nThis supports intentional edge bleed and crop layouts; the image payload,\neffects, crop, and relationship remain source-owned.\n\nStale hash, ambiguous target, unsupported field, unsafe relationship change,\ncross-object mutation, or topology rewrite must fail. Global voice changes require explicit scope and a full-deck\neditorial review.\n---TABLES---\n# Charts and tables\n\nChoose the visual from the relationship the audience must understand.\n\n| Relationship | Prefer |\n| --- | --- |\n| trend or change over ordered time | line, area, or ordered columns |\n| changing composition and total magnitude over ordered time | streamgraph |\n| magnitude across categories | bars or columns with a common baseline |\n| small exact counts where one repeated glyph has a declared unit | pictographic bar or column |\n| distribution or correlation | scatter, bubble, or distribution view |\n| intensity across two categorical dimensions | heatmap |\n| open/high/low/close movement over ordered periods | candlestick |\n| hierarchical part-to-whole allocation | treemap |\n| hierarchical part-to-whole path across concentric levels | sunburst |\n| conserved magnitude moving through a directed process | sankey |\n| multivariate profile across a small shared scale | standard radar |\n| contribution to change | waterfall |\n| precise lookup or rule comparison | table |\n| mixed measures sharing a truthful category axis | deliberate combo chart |\n\nAvoid pies with many categories, decorative 3D, dual axes without a necessary\nand clearly labelled relationship, truncated scales that exaggerate change,\nand a chart that merely repeats one large number.\n\n## Evidence integrity\n\n- Preserve source values, units, time windows, denominators, and uncertainty.\n- Use direct labels where they reduce legend lookup.\n- Keep common scales for comparisons that claim comparability.\n- Show missing values and estimates honestly.\n- Put the exact source and as-of date on the page or in a visible source area.\n\nTreat native data-label defaults as unsafe. /Users/zfang/workspace/officekit-main-skill-eval-20260903/evals/presentation-skill-ablation/common/references/scenarios/analysis-decision.md ---\n# Scenario: analysis and decision\n\n## Audience task\n\nHelp an informed audience compare evidence, understand tradeoffs, and make a\nspecific decision. The deck should reduce uncertainty rather than manufacture\nconfidence.\n\nLock the decision, criteria, time horizon, baseline, and uncertainty before\ndrawing. Every recommendation must point to evidence or an explicit assumption.\nCounter-evidence belongs near the claim it limits.\n\n## Narrative\n\nFrame the decision, establish criteria, show the evidence and alternatives,\nsurface uncertainty, recommend a path, then make the next decision explicit.\nPut decisive evidence before the recommendation. Use an appendix for audit\ndetail, not for facts required to understand the choice.\n\nUseful page jobs include decision frame, baseline, driver analysis, option\ncomparison, sensitivity or scenario range, recommendation, conditions, and\nnext action. Do not force all of them into one fixed sequence.\n\n## Density and rhythm\n\nAlternate compact decision frames with denser evidence pages. Preserve common\nscales across comparable charts. Give exceptions and uncertainty enough space\nto be read. A live deck may stage a complex driver chain; a reader deck must\nremain self-contained without the animation.\n\n## Relationship-to-carrier choices\n\n- annotated trend, variance, waterfall, or distribution chart;\n- option comparison on shared criteria and a common visual scale;\n- driver tree, causal chain, or sensitivity map;\n- evidence table with one decision-relevant row or threshold highlighted;\n- recommendation page with conditions, trigger, owner, and next action;\n- scenario range rather than a single false-precision forecast.\n\nCharts should encode a relationship, not decorate a number. Tables work when\nexact values or criteria matter. Diagrams work when causal structure matters.\nUse sourced imagery only when the physical context changes the decision; do not\nuse a generic market image as the evidence carrier.\n\n## Visual grammar\n\nUse restrained surfaces, straight geometry, explicit axes, thin dividers, and\none high-contrast decision role. Prefer direct labels, aligned baselines, and\nconsistent units. Use boxes only when they encode comparable alternatives or\nbounded states. Connectors must carry direction, dependency, or causality.\n\nTypography should separate claim, evidence annotation, and source. Spacing\nshould make the decision path scannable without turning every observation into\na card. Motifs may mark thresholds or selected options, but must not become a\nsecond legend.\n\nFor a bar-line or other combo chart, preserve one truthful category or time\nplot when the comparison depends on it. Keep the line and markers above pale or\ntransparent bars, reserve clearance around every marker, and re-anchor only the\nlabels that collide. Split into aligned panels only when sharing a plot would\nmisrepresent the units or remains illegible after those repairs; never split\nmerely to silence an overlap warning.\n\n## Avoid\n\nDashboard walls, ornamental KPI cards, incomparable scales, decorative arrows,\nequal emphasis on every metric, recommendations before evidence, hidden\nuncertainty, and confidence language unsupported by the source.\n\n## Review questions\n\n- Can the audience state the decision, criteria, and uncertainty after a scan?\n- Does each visual change the decision, or merely decorate a number?\n- Can every line, marker, value label, axis, interval, and error bar be traced\n  without another series obscuring it?\n- Are counter-evidence and assumptions visible before the conclusion?\n- Is the requested action explicit, bounded, and supported?\n- If the page feels generic, should the claim/evidence or carrier change before\n  palette and styling are adjusted?\n--- /Users/zfang/workspace/officekit-main-skill-eval-20260903/evals/presentation-skill-ablation/common/references/import.md ---\nsed: /Users/zfang/workspace/officekit-main-skill-eval-20260903/evals/presentation-skill-ablation/common/references/import.md: No such file or directory\n--- /Users/zfang/workspace/officekit-main-skill-eval-20260903/evals/presentation-skill-ablation/common/references/charts.md ---\nsed: /Users/zfang/workspace/officekit-main-skill-eval-20260903/evals/presentation-skill-ablation/common/references/charts.md: No such file or directory\n--- /Users/zfang/workspace/officekit-main-skill-eval-20260903/evals/presentation-skill-ablation/common/references/text.md ---\n# Audience-facing text\n\nPresentation copy is spoken or scanned under time pressure. Preserve facts,\nsources, numbers, qualifiers, names, and user-locked wording before editing\nstyle.\n\nUse this editorial sequence:\n\n```text\nlock facts and sources\n→ state the audience outcome\n→ write the page claim\n→ add only support needed for that claim\n→ fit copy to the rendered page\n→ review the whole-deck voice\n```\n\n## Write for the page job\n\n- Prefer a conclusion or useful question over a topic label.\n- Make the title and dominant visual agree; do not repeat the same sentence in\n  title, body, and callout.\n- Keep one visible hierarchy: claim, evidence, annotation, source.\n- Use direct verbs and concrete nouns. Remove throat-clearing, slogans,\n  abstract stacks, and redundant contrast patterns such as repeated\n  “not X but Y”.\n- Keep uncertainty and scope close to the claim they qualify.\n- Put detailed derivation in notes or an appendix only when the visible page\n  remains understandable without it.\n\nSimple PPJ text is a string. Mixed formatting uses `paragraphs[]` and `runs[]`.\nDo not put Markdown, HTML, CSS, or invented inline markup into a text string.\nAssign language and font roles explicitly for mixed-script runs.\n\n## Keep the talk track in speaker notes\n\nUse `pages[].notes` for the spoken bridge, caveat, source detail, or facilitation\nprompt that a live presenter needs but the audience should not read on the\ncanvas. Notes use the same `textContent` contract as visible text: a string for\nsimple prose, or paragraphs and runs when emphasis or language boundaries\nmatter. Notes supplement the page; they do not excuse an ambiguous visible\nclaim or hide evidence required for a reader deck.\n\nImported notes remain source-bound. When the page `nativeRef` issues\n`setNotes`, an Agent may change plain text or the text inside an existing rich\nrun topology. Keep paragraph/run counts, IDs, styles, and representation kind\nunchanged. A notes-absent capable page accepts one plain string. NotesMaster,\nlayout, fields, hyperlinks, picture bullets, arbitrary notes shapes, and\nrelationship topology remain native-owned and must not be reconstructed.\n\nFor mixed-script text, make the language boundary explicit where shaping,\nfont fallback, spell checking, or accessibility depends on it:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"runs\": [\n    { \"text\": \"关键结论\", \"style\": { \"language\": \"zh-CN\", \"font\": \"body-cjk\" } },\n    { \"text\": \" / Evidence\", \"style\": { \"language\": \"en-US\", \"font\": \"body-latin\" } }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\nUse a bounded BCP-47 tag; do not invent tags from font names or locale display\nlabels. Language and typeface solve different problems, so setting one does not\nauthorize guessing the other. Imported direct run language is editable only\nthrough an issued `fontLanguage` leaf.\n\n## Use native formulas for mathematical evidence\n\nKeep prose in ordinary runs and put only the mathematical expression in a\nformula run. Do not include `\\(` or `\\)` delimiters:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"runs\": [\n    { \"text\": \"Expected loss: \" },\n    {\n      \"id\": \"loss-equation\",\n      \"formula\": {\n        \"syntax\": \"latex\",\n        \"source\": \"\\\\sum_{i=1}^{n} p_i \\\\cdot L_i\"\n      },\n      \"style\": { \"size\": 24, \"color\": \"#172033\" }\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\nThe supported subset covers literals, groups, subscript and superscript,\nfractions, square roots, common Greek letters and symbols, integral/sum/product,\nroman text, common functions, bounded spacing, and ordinary left/right\ndelimiters. It does not execute TeX: macros, environments, packages,\nconditionals, counters, I/O, matrices, alignment, color commands and unknown\ncommands fail before output. Limits are 4,096 source characters, 512 tokens, 32\nnesting levels and 2,048 AST nodes.\n\nA formula run may declare only `size` and solid `color`; it cannot carry a\nhyperlink, font override, highlight, gradient, shadow or text decoration.\nOfficeKit writes editable native Office Math (`a14:m` with OMML), not an image,\nformula font or literal backslash fallback.\n\nExact LaTeX recovery comes from an OfficeKit-authored PPTX's embedded PPJ.\nThird-party OMML stays source-owned and is never reverse-translated into guessed\nLaTeX. Do not mutate an imported formula unless a future explicit source-bound\ncapability says that exact operation is safe.\n\n## Use opacity as hierarchy, not camouflage\n\nPPJ text colors accept eight-digit HEX or a declared color token with `alpha`:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"text\": \"Source: audited operations ledger\",\n  \"style\": {\n    \"defaultText\": { \"color\": \"#16324FB8\", \"size\": 9 }\n  }\n}\n```\n\nThe compiler writes one editable native text-color alpha value. Use it for\nsecondary annotation, metadata, or text over a controlled image overlay. Keep\nclaims, critical values, and source obligations readable at the intended\ndelivery distance. Opacity does not repair weak contrast, a busy photograph,\nor an unclear hierarchy; adjust the background or composition first.\n\nImported text opacity may be visible in projected PPJ, but changing source\nformatting still requires an issued capability. A text-replacement capability\ndoes not authorize a color or opacity edit.\n\n## Reserve gradient and shadow for display text\n\nPPJ can author one native linear or centered-radial text gradient and one\nnative outer shadow on a run or `defaultText` style:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"text\": \"Annual signal\",\n  \"style\": {\n    \"defaultText\": {\n      \"size\": 34,\n      \"gradient\": {\n        \"kind\": \"linear\",\n        \"angle\": 18,\n        \"stops\": [\n          { \"offset\": 0, \"color\": \"#16324F\" },\n          { \"offset\": 1, \"color\": \"#0B8F8F\", \"opacity\": 0.82 }\n        ]\n      },\n      \"shadow\": {\n        \"color\": \"#16324F66\",\n        \"blur\": 3,\n        \"distance\": 1.5,\n        \"angle\": 90\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\nUse this treatment for a short hero title, launch wordmark, or one display\nnumber when it reinforces the deck's design grammar. Keep body copy, sources,\naxes, labels, and evidence text solid. A style cannot declare both `color` and\n`gradient`; resolve the paint choice explicitly. Do not use shadow to rescue\npoor contrast or place legible text over a busy image. Render the actual slide\nand verify the thinnest glyph strokes at delivery size.\n\nThe compiler writes editable DrawingML text paint and outer-shadow state, not\na rasterized title. Canonical imported gradients and shadows project back into\nPPJ, while theme-transformed gradients, glow, reflection, inner shadow,\nWordArt, and irregular effect graphs remain source-owned. A projected effect\ndoes not by itself grant permission to mutate third-party formatting; follow\nthe issued `nativeRef` capability.\n\n## Style bullets as text, not decoration\n\nCharacter and numbered bullets may use the same deck-local color tokens and\nalpha-bearing literals as other authored text:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"style\": {\n    \"bullet\": {\n      \"type\": \"character\",\n      \"character\": \"•\",\n      \"color\": { \"token\": \"signal\", \"alpha\": 0.72 },\n      \"sizePercent\": 0.9\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\nA PPJ palette token resolves to its declared RGB/alpha; it does not silently\nclaim a native PowerPoint theme identity. Keep bullets subordinate to their\ntext and use indentation, baseline and spacing for hierarchy. Do not turn each\nbullet into a badge, pill or card.\n\n## Highlight only the evidence that needs it\n\nUse `highlight` on a run when the audience must locate a short phrase, changed\nassumption, threshold, or review finding inside otherwise continuous text:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"text\": {\n    \"paragraphs\": [{\n      \"runs\": [\n        { \"text\": \"Decision: \" },\n        { \"text\": \"proceed only above 84%\", \"style\": { \"highlight\": \"#FFF2CC\" } }\n      ]\n    }]\n  }\n}\n```\n\nHighlight is editable native text state. It is not a pill, badge, card, or a\nsubstitute for hierarchy. Keep the marked span short and use one highlight\nlogic consistently across the deck. Authored highlight must be opaque; choose\na lighter color instead of asking alpha to repair contrast.\n\nImported direct RGB highlights project into `run.style.highlight`. Theme-bound\nhighlights remain source-owned and are changed only through an issued\n`fontHighlightScheme` leaf so PPJ does not flatten a source theme into guessed\nRGB.\n\n## Fit without shrinking the argument\n\nRespect the page's content budget. If text does not fit, remove duplication,\nsplit the page by audience task, change the carrier, or move audit detail to a\nsupporting page. Tiny type is not a valid layout repair.\n\nAfter every meaningful copy edit, rebuild and render the affected pages. Check\nline breaks, widows, CJK punctuation, number/unit binding, source visibility,\nand whether the new wording changed the intended visual emphasis.\n\nLocal edits stay local. A request to change one title does not authorize a\ndeck-wide rewrite.
